cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is waging war against Judah. So Zedekiah, king of Judah, sends two men to the prophet Jeremiah: Pashhur son of Malchijah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. They've come with a request.

cards.question: With Babylon at war against them, what do Zedekiah's men ask Jeremiah to do?

answers.text: Inquire of the LORD for them
Make peace with Babylon for them
Lead the army out for them

cards.question: Zedekiah's men hope the LORD will do something like all His past ___, so Nebuchadnezzar will pull back.

cards.text: Zedekiah's men are hoping for a wonder, and I know that feeling: every time my old junk drawer rattled open, I held my breath and thought, THIS is it! Jeremiah answers with a message for Zedekiah from the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.question: The Chaldeans besiege the city from outside the wall, and Zedekiah's people are fighting them. What does the LORD say He will turn against Zedekiah's people?

answers.text: The weapons in their own hands
The walls of their own city
The horses in their own stables

cards.question: The LORD says He Himself will fight for Zedekiah against Babylon.

cards.text: The LORD says He will strike down the people of the city, both man and beast. They will die in a terrible plague.

cards.question: After the plague, the LORD says He will hand Zedekiah, his officers and the survivors over to Nebuchadnezzar. Nebuchadnezzar will show them pity.

cards.text: Then a message for the people. The LORD says, 'Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.' Two roads, friend, and NO third one marked 'I'll get back to You.'

cards.question: With the Chaldeans besieging the city, who does the LORD say will live?
The LORD says He has set His face against the city and will hand it to the king of Babylon. What will that king do to it?

cards.text: Next, the LORD has a word for the royal family, the house of David. And friend, this job comes with an alarm clock and NO snooze button.

cards.question: Every morning, the house of David is told to administer ___ and rescue the victim of robbery from his oppressor.
If the house of David doesn't administer justice every morning and rescue the victim of robbery, the LORD says His wrath will burn like fire with no one to put it out.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He is against the ones who live above the valley, atop the rocky plateau. Friend, I spent years at the bottom of a junk drawer, so living up high sounds AMAZING to me.

cards.question: The LORD says He is against the ones who dwell above the valley, atop the rocky plateau. What do they say about themselves?

answers.text: No one can come against us
The LORD will always protect us
Egypt will come to save us

cards.text: The LORD says He will punish them as their deeds deserve, with a fire in their forest that consumes everything around them. So much for "Who can come against us?"

Now the LORD sends Jeremiah down to the palace of the king of Judah, who sits on David's throne, with a word for the king, his officials and his people. Jeremiah's making a house call, friend, and the house is a PALACE.
Sound familiar? Administer justice and righteousness, and rescue the victim of robbery from the hand of his oppressor.

cards.question: The LORD also tells the king to do no wrong or violence to certain people. Who are they?

answers.text: Foreigners and the fatherless and widows

cards.text: And one more: "Do not shed innocent blood in this place." Then the LORD gives the king a big IF.

cards.question: If the king carries out the LORD's commands to do justice, rescue the oppressed and not shed innocent blood, kings who sit on David's throne will enter the palace gates riding on chariots and horses.

cards.text: Then the other side of that IF. The LORD swears by Himself, and friend, He has no one greater to swear by (Hebrews 6:13).

cards.question: If the king doesn't obey, what does the LORD swear this palace will become?

cards.text: The LORD tells the king's house, "You are like Gilead to Me, like the summit of Lebanon". A MOUNTAINTOP, friend. Nobody ever called me a mountaintop. Best I ever got was "huh, it still works."

cards.question: Even so, the LORD says He will turn the king's house into a desert, like cities where no one lives.
The LORD will appoint destroyers who cut down the choicest ___ of the king's house and throw them into the ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD says many nations will pass by the city and ask one another, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?'

cards.question: When the nations ask why the LORD did this to the great city, what answer do people give?

answers.text: They forsook the LORD's covenant and served other gods
Their king lost a war to a stronger king
Their walls were built too low to hold back an army

findings.problem: The Chaldeans appear here for the first time, in the question itself, with no word on who they are. They are the Babylonians, but the baker hasn't been told that.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: No card covers the second half of Jeremiah 21:4: the LORD will gather the enemy's forces in the center of the city. The baker leaves without this detail of the judgment.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This story card has 3 sentences. Only the opening card may go past 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The 'alarm clock and NO snooze button' joke depends on the 'every morning' command, but the baker hasn't heard that yet. It first shows up in the next card's question. 'This job' also points to a duty that hasn't been named, so the joke won't click when it's read.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The card quotes "Who can come against us?", which comes from Jeremiah 21:13, but it cites only Jeremiah 21:14.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The text says the king's house is LIKE Gilead and LIKE the summit of Lebanon. The reaction 'A MOUNTAINTOP' and 'Nobody ever called me a mountaintop' drop the 'like' and treat the house as if it were called a mountaintop. They also turn the two pictures into one, and Gilead isn't a summit.

'Best I ever got was "huh, it still works"' makes up a new fact about his past. It also goes against the backstory: his kids called him Papa, and 'Of every name Papa Dorin has ever been called, Papa is the best one.'

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The question asks why the LORD did this, and only the right answer mentions the LORD at all. It is also the only one in Bible language ('forsook the LORD's covenant'). The wrong answers are worldly reasons and don't answer a question about the LORD's reason, and 'walls were built too low' is close to silly. So the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
